angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,298,872 km at 76.86 pc = 0.23 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 13.0107 +/- 0.0172 mas (same row, RUWE 0.99): 76.86 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.867 +/- 0.033 solar radii from Addison et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-257 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.502.3704A/abstract): 1,298,872 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.407 +/- 0.045 solar masses from Addison et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-257 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.502.3704A/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6095 +/- 89 K from Addison et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-257 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.502.3704A/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Addison et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-257 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021MNRAS.502.3704A/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-257.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.044, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
